statement: For events A and B, provided that P(B) ≠ 0, Bayes' theorem (or Bayes' rule) is given by P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A)P(A)}{P(B)}.

symbols.meaning: conditional probability or likelihood of B given A
posterior probability of A given B

properties.why: When the conditioning event B is fixed, its probability P(B) in the denominator is constant with respect to varying A.

properties.property: Denominator expansion via law of total probability: P(B) = P(B|A)P(A) + P(B|¬A)P(¬A)
properties.why: The denominator probability of the evidence can be calculated by summing over a partition of the space.
Dividing P(A|B) by P(¬A|B) cancels out P(B), relating posterior odds to prior odds multiplied by the likelihood ratio (Bayes factor).

properties.property: Continuous random variable density form: f_{X|Y=y}(x) = \frac{f_{Y|X=x}(y)f_X(x)}{f_Y(y)}
properties.why: Analogously derived from the definitions of conditional density f_{X|Y=y}(x) = f_{X,Y}(x,y)/f_Y(y) and f_{Y|X=x}(y) = f_{X,Y}(x,y)/f_X(x).

properties.property: Three-event conditioned form: P(A|B ∩ C) = \frac{P(B|A ∩ C)P(A|C)}{P(B|C)}
properties.why: Obtained by expanding P(A ∩ B ∩ C) via the chain rule conditioned on C with P(C) > 0.

assumptions.breaks_when: The conditioning event B has zero probability, making the denominator zero and conditional probability undefined.

assumptions.assumption: x and y lie within the support of continuous random variables X and Y, with f_X(x) > 0 and f_Y(y) > 0
assumptions.breaks_when: Evaluating outside the support where marginal density f_Y(y) = 0.

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero resulting in an undefined posterior probability.
failure_modes.cause: The evidence event B has probability P(B) = 0 (or density f_Y(y) = 0).

failure_modes.mode: Base rate fallacy / False positive paradox
failure_modes.signature: Posterior probability P(A|B) remains surprisingly low despite a high true positive rate P(B|A).
failure_modes.cause: Extremely low prior probability P(A) relative to the false positive rate P(B|¬A), causing the denominator to be dominated by false positives.
